mnemonic: It is composed of 单 (single) and 词 (word). Think of it as 'a single word'. Don't confuse 单词 (a word) with 字 (zì), 'a character'. For 'vocabulary' as a whole, you can also say 词汇 (cíhuì).
examples: - 我每天学十个新单词。 = I learn ten new words every day.
- 这个单词是什么意思？ = What does this word mean?
- 请把这个单词写下来。 = Please write this word down.
- 他的单词量很大。 = His vocabulary is large.

mnemonic: It is composed of 表 (show) and 达 (reach). Think of it as 'making your thoughts reach others'. Don't confuse 表达 (an expression in language) with 表现 (biǎoxiàn), which means 'performance' or 'behavior'.
examples: - 这个表达很地道。 = This expression sounds very natural.
- 你能用中文表达你的想法吗？ = Can you express your ideas in Chinese?
- 我不知道怎么表达我的感受。 = I don't know how to express my feelings.
- 请教我一些有用的表达。 = Please teach me some useful expressions.

mnemonic: It is composed of 发 (emit) and 音 (sound). Think of it as 'sending out a sound'. Same characters as the Korean 발음 and the Japanese 発音 (the simplified 发 is the same as 発).
examples: - 你的发音很好。 = Your pronunciation is good.
- 汉语的发音不太难。 = Chinese pronunciation is not too difficult.
- 老师纠正了我的发音。 = My teacher corrected my pronunciation.
- 请注意发音和声调。 = Please pay attention to pronunciation and tones.

mnemonic: It is composed of 死 (die) and 亡 (perish). The single character 死 (sǐ) is the verb 'to die'. Because 四 (sì, four) sounds almost like 死 (sǐ), the number 4 is considered unlucky in Chinese culture.
examples: - 人人都会面对死亡。 = Everyone will face death.
- 爷爷的死亡让全家人很难过。 = Grandpa's death made the whole family sad.
- 他并不害怕死亡。 = He is not afraid of death.
- 这场事故造成了两人死亡。 = The accident caused two deaths.

mnemonic: It is composed of 疾 (illness) and 病 (sickness). Both have the 疒 radical (a person lying in a sickbed). 疾病 is formal; in everyday speech, say 病 (bìng) or 生病 (shēngbìng), 'to get sick'.
examples: - 他因为疾病请假了。 = He asked for leave because of illness.
- 这种疾病很少见。 = This disease is rare.
- 预防疾病很重要。 = Preventing disease is important.
- 运动可以预防很多疾病。 = Exercise can prevent many diseases.

mnemonic: It is composed of 禁 (prohibit) and 忌 (avoid). Same characters as the Korean 금기 and the Japanese 禁忌. A famous Chinese taboo: giving a clock (送钟, sòngzhōng) sounds like 送终 (attending a funeral).
examples: - 在中国，送钟是一种禁忌。 = In China, giving a clock as a gift is a taboo.
- 谈论死亡在有些家庭是禁忌。 = Talking about death is taboo in some families.
- 这种药是孕妇的禁忌。 = This medicine is contraindicated for pregnant women.
- 不同的文化有不同的禁忌。 = Different cultures have different taboos.

mnemonic: It is composed of 例 (example) and 子 (a noun suffix, 'child'). The neutral-tone 子 is added to many nouns. 例如 (lìrú) means 'for example'.
examples: - 请举一个例子。 = Please give an example.
- 水果有很多，例如苹果和香蕉。 = There are many fruits, for example apples and bananas.
- 这个句子是一个好例子。 = This sentence is a good example.
- 你能给我一个例子吗？ = Can you give me an example?

mnemonic: It is composed of 数 (count) and 字 (character). Be careful! 数 is read shù as a noun, but shǔ as a verb: 数一数 (shǔ yi shǔ), 'to count'. In China, 8 (bā) is lucky because it sounds like 发 (fā), 'to get rich'.
examples: - 我记不住这个电话号码的数字。 = I can't remember the digits of this phone number.
- 八在中国是一个吉利的数字。 = Eight is a lucky number in China.
- 他对数字很敏感。 = He is sensitive to numbers.
- 请在黑板上写数字。 = Please write the numbers on the blackboard.

mnemonic: It is composed of 一 (one), 部 (section) and 分 (portion). Think of it as 'one portion of a whole'. Its opposite is 全部 (quánbù), 'all, the whole'.
examples: - 一部分人不同意。 = Some people disagree.
- 我只读了这本书的一部分。 = I only read a part of this book.
- 这只是一部分原因。 = This is only part of the reason.
- 机器的一部分坏了。 = A part of the machine is broken.

mnemonic: It is composed of 建 (build) and 筑 (construct). It means both 'a building' and 'architecture'. For a multi-story building, you can also say 楼 (lóu) or 大楼 (dàlóu), and the formal 'building' is 建筑物 (jiànzhùwù).
examples: - 那座建筑是图书馆。 = That building is a library.
- 这个城市有很多古老的建筑。 = This city has many old buildings.
- 车站旁边有一座高大的建筑。 = There is a tall building next to the station.
- 他是研究建筑的。 = He studies architecture.

mnemonic: It is composed of 字 (character) and 母 (mother). Think of it as 'the mother of characters'. For 'the alphabet', say 字母表 (zìmǔbiǎo). Chinese pinyin (拼音) is written with these Latin letters, and F is read like 'ef'.
examples: - F是英语字母表的第六个字母。 = F is the sixth letter of the English alphabet.
- 你能背出所有字母吗？ = Can you recite all the letters?
- 我的名字以F开头。 = My name starts with F.
- 这是字母F。 = This is the letter F.

mnemonic: It is composed of 汉 (Han, the main ethnic group of China) and 字 (character). It is the source of the Korean 한자 (hanja) and the Japanese 漢字 (kanji). Mainland China uses simplified characters (简体字), while Taiwan uses traditional ones (繁體字).
examples: - 我在学汉字。 = I am studying Chinese characters.
- 这个汉字怎么读？ = How do you read this character?
- 汉语有很多汉字。 = Chinese has many characters.
- 汉字起源于中国。 = Chinese characters originated in China.

mnemonic: It is composed of 相似 (resemble each other) and 性 (nature). Think of it as 'the nature of resembling'. The adjective is 相似 (xiāngsì), and the verb 'to resemble' is 像 (xiàng).
examples: - 这两种语言有相似性。 = These two languages have similarities.
- 我惊讶于日语和韩语的相似性。 = I was surprised by the similarity between Japanese and Korean.
- 语法的相似性帮助我们学习。 = Grammatical similarity helps us learn.
- 我要调查这两个案件的相似性。 = I will investigate the similarity between the two cases.

mnemonic: It is composed of 国 (country) and 家 (home/family). Think of it as 'a country as a big family-home'. The same word is used for 'nation' in Japanese 国家 (こっか).
examples: - 你是哪个国家的人？ = Which country are you from?
- 中国是一个大国家。 = China is a big country.
- 世界上有很多国家。 = There are many countries in the world.
- 我的国家很热。 = My country is hot.

mnemonic: It is composed of 计 (calculate) and 划 (map out). Think of it as 'calculating and mapping out'. It works as both a noun and a verb. Don't confuse 计划 (a plan) with 打算 (dǎsuan), 'to intend'.
examples: - 我在做旅行计划。 = I am making travel plans.
- 一切按计划进行。 = Everything is proceeding as planned.
- 我来说明新计划。 = I will explain the new plan.
- 暑假你有什么计划？ = What are your plans for summer vacation?

mnemonic: It is composed of 自 (self) and 己 (oneself). It is the everyday word for 'oneself'. The formal 自身 (zìshēn) is closer to the Korean 자신. Don't confuse it with 自信 (zìxìn), 'confidence'.
examples: - 要相信自己。 = Believe in yourself.
- 我自己去。 = I will go myself.
- 他自己也不知道。 = Even he himself doesn't know.
- 这是你自己的问题。 = This is your own problem.

tr: （zhùyì）- Attention; to pay attention, to be careful
mnemonic: It is composed of 注 (pour/focus) and 意 (mind). Think of it as 'pouring your mind into something'. It is a verb and a noun. Same characters as the Japanese 注意.
examples: - 请注意脚下。 = Please watch your step.
- 老师提醒我要注意安全。 = The teacher reminded me to be careful about safety.
- 过马路要注意车。 = Watch out for cars when crossing the road.
- 你要注意身体。 = Take care of your health.

mnemonic: It is composed of 文 (writing/literature) and 化 (transform). Think of it as 'what writing and change build over time'. Same characters as the Korean 문화 and the Japanese 文化.
examples: - 我对中国文化很感兴趣。 = I am very interested in Chinese culture.
- 饮食文化因国家而不同。 = Food culture differs by country.
- 我在学习文化差异。 = I am learning about cultural differences.
- 我喜欢韩国文化。 = I like Korean culture.

mnemonic: It is composed of 方 (direction) and 面 (face/side). Think of it as 'the direction a face points'. The single character 面 (miàn) means 'surface, face', and also 'noodles' (面条, miàntiáo). Use 在...方面 for 'in terms of...'.
examples: - 这件事有好的一面，也有坏的一面。 = This matter has a good side and a bad side.
- 他在很多方面都很出色。 = He is outstanding in many respects.
- 从另一个方面来看。 = Looking at it from another aspect.
- 在学习方面，我需要帮助。 = In terms of studying, I need help.

mnemonic: Think of the four dots at the bottom (灬) as 'dots'. 点 is very versatile: a point (优点, yōudiǎn, 'strong point'), a dot, and the hour (两点, liǎng diǎn, '2 o'clock'). It also appears in 一点 (yìdiǎn), 'a little', and 有点 (yǒudiǎn), 'a bit'.
examples: - 这一点很重要。 = This point is important.
- 请用线把点连起来。 = Please connect the dots with lines.
- 他的优点是很勤奋。 = His strong point is that he is hardworking.
- 我们两点见面。 = We will meet at two o'clock.

mnemonic: It is composed of 早 (early) and 上 (up/on). Think of it as 'early up'. Unlike the Korean 아침, 早上 means only 'morning'. For 'breakfast', say 早饭 (zǎofàn) or 早餐 (zǎocān).
examples: - 我每天早上六点起床。 = I get up at six every morning.
- 你吃早饭了吗？ = Have you had breakfast?
- 今天早上很冷。 = It was cold this morning.
- 早上我很忙。 = I am busy in the morning.

mnemonic: It is a sound-based borrowing of the English 'coffee'. Notice that both 咖 and 啡 have the 口 (mouth) radical, a hint that they are used for their sound and for something you taste. No nosebleed pun here, unlike in Korean!
examples: - 我每天早上喝咖啡。 = I drink coffee every morning.
- 你的咖啡要加糖吗？ = Do you want sugar in your coffee?
- 请给我一杯热咖啡。 = A hot coffee, please.
- 比起咖啡，我更喜欢茶。 = I prefer tea to coffee.

mnemonic: It is composed of 韩 (Korea) and 国 (country). Don't confuse 韩国 (Korea) with 中国 (Zhōngguó), 'China'. The language is 韩语 (Hányǔ) and a Korean person is 韩国人 (Hánguórén). Taiwan writes it as 韓國.
examples: - 我想去韩国。 = I want to go to Korea.
- 我在学习韩语。 = I am studying Korean.
- 我非常喜欢韩国菜。 = I really like Korean food.
- 我的朋友是韩国人。 = My friend is Korean.

mnemonic: It is composed of 咖啡 (coffee) and 馆 (a public venue). You can find 馆 in 图书馆 (túshūguǎn), 'library', 饭馆 (fànguǎn), 'restaurant', and 博物馆 (bówùguǎn), 'museum'. A tea house is 茶馆 (cháguǎn).
examples: - 我在咖啡馆见朋友。 = I meet my friend at a cafe.
- 这家咖啡馆很安静。 = This cafe is quiet.
- 我喜欢在咖啡馆学习。 = I like studying at cafes.
- 车站附近有一家咖啡馆。 = There is a cafe near the station.

mnemonic: It is composed of 朋 (two 月 side by side, 'companions') and 友 (friend). Think of it as 'two people side by side'. The second syllable has a neutral tone: péngyou. Also used for 'boyfriend/girlfriend' in 男朋友 and 女朋友.
examples: - 我和朋友一起看电影。 = I watch a movie with my friend.
- 他是我的好朋友。 = He is my good friend.
- 我有很多朋友。 = I have many friends.
- 我给朋友打电话。 = I call my friend.

mnemonic: It is composed of 周 (week) and 末 (end). Think of it as 'the end of the week'. Same characters as the Korean 주말 and the Japanese 週末 (simplified 周 vs traditional 週). The days are 星期一 (xīngqīyī), Monday, and so on.
examples: - 你周末做什么？ = What do you do on the weekend?
- 周末我和朋友出去玩。 = On the weekend I go out with friends.
- 上个周末我在家。 = I was at home last weekend.
- 我盼着周末。 = I am looking forward to the weekend.

tr: （shuō）- To speak, to say, to talk
mnemonic: It is composed of 讠 (the speech radical) and 兑. Think of it as 'words coming out'. To talk about a subject or give a talk, 讲 (jiǎng) is also used. For 'to speak' in conversation, 说话 (shuōhuà) is common.
examples: - 请说中文。 = Please speak Chinese.
- 我和朋友在电话里说话。 = I talk with my friend on the phone.
- 我有话想对老师说。 = There is something I want to say to the teacher.
- 他会说英语。 = He can speak English.

mnemonic: It is composed of 避 (evade) and 免 (be spared). Think of it as 'to evade so as to be spared'. To physically dodge or step aside, use 避开 (bìkāi), and to hide from someone, use 躲 (duǒ).
examples: - 我尽量避免高峰时间。 = I try to avoid rush hour.
- 为了避免迟到，我早点出门。 = To avoid being late, I leave home early.
- 请避免走危险的路。 = Please avoid taking dangerous roads.
- 他好像在躲着我。 = He seems to be avoiding me.

mnemonic: It is composed of 想 (think) and 起来 (come up). Think of it as 'a thought coming up'. Don't confuse 想起来 (suddenly recall) with 记得 (jìde), 'to remember' (still having it in memory).
examples: - 听到这首歌，我想起了过去。 = When I hear this song, I recall the past.
- 我想不起来他的名字。 = I can't remember his name.
- 我想起了小时候。 = I recalled my childhood.
- 我想起来作业还没写。 = I just remembered I haven't done my homework.

mnemonic: It is composed of 亻 (person) and 故. 做 is the all-purpose verb 'to make' or 'to do': 做饭 (cook), 做作业 (do homework). To manufacture, use 制造 (zhìzào), and to build, 造 (zào).
examples: - 妈妈每天做饭。 = My mother cooks every day.
- 我和朋友一起做了蛋糕。 = I made a cake with my friend.
- 我用纸做了一个盒子。 = I made a box out of paper.
- 他做了一个新计划。 = He made a new plan.

mnemonic: 用 is a very common character, and also works as 'with' or 'by means of': 用中文说 (say it in Chinese). The formal word is 使用 (shǐyòng), the exact match for the Korean 사용하다.
examples: - 我用筷子吃饭。 = I eat with chopsticks.
- 我可以用这支笔吗？ = May I use this pen?
- 我每天都使用手机。 = I use my phone every day.
- 请合理使用时间。 = Please use your time wisely.

mnemonic: It is composed of 意味 (meaning/flavor) and 着 (a particle showing an ongoing state). Think of it as 'carrying the flavor of an idea'. For the noun 'meaning', say 意思 (yìsi): 这是什么意思？
examples: - 红色意味着危险。 = Red means danger.
- 这句话意味着感谢。 = This sentence signifies gratitude.
- 沉默不意味着同意。 = Silence does not mean agreement.
- 失败并不意味着结束。 = Failure does not mean the end.

tr: （dàngzuò）- To regard as, to treat as
mnemonic: It is composed of 当 (treat as) and 作 (make). Think of it as 'to make something be treated as something else', used with 把: 把A当作B. The formal versions are 视为 (shìwéi) and 看作 (kànzuò), and 认为 (rènwéi) means 'to think that'.
examples: - 我把他当作朋友。 = I regard him as a friend.
- 别把这当作玩笑。 = Don't treat this as a joke.
- 他把我当作自己的孩子。 = He treats me as his own child.
- 我把这次经历当作宝贵的财富。 = I regard this experience as a precious asset.

mnemonic: It is composed of 拜 (bow/pay respects) and 访 (visit). Think of it as 'paying respects by visiting'. It is polite, used for visiting people. For tourist sites, use 参观 (cānguān), and for official visits or interviews, 访问 (fǎngwèn).
examples: - 我去拜访了老师。 = I went to visit my teacher.
- 下周我要拜访一位客户。 = Next week I will visit a client.
- 拜访朋友前我会先打电话。 = I call before visiting a friend.
- 他明天要来拜访我们。 = He is coming to visit us tomorrow.

tr: （qīngxié）- To tilt, to slant, to lean
mnemonic: It is composed of 倾 (lean) and 斜 (slanted). Like the Korean 기울이다, 倾 also appears in 倾听 (qīngtīng), 'to listen attentively', and 倾注 (qīngzhù), 'to pour (effort) into'.
examples: - 请把杯子稍微倾斜一点。 = Please tilt the cup a little.
- 这座塔有点倾斜。 = This tower leans a little.
- 我认真倾听老师的话。 = I listen attentively to the teacher.
- 他把全部精力倾注在工作上。 = He pours all his energy into his work.

mnemonic: It is composed of 理 (reason) and 解 (untie). Think of it as 'untying the reason'. Same characters as the Japanese 理解. For plain 'I get it', use 懂 (dǒng) or 明白 (míngbai).
examples: - 我理解了汉语的语法。 = I understood Chinese grammar.
- 我无法理解他的心情。 = I can't understand his feelings.
- 听了解释，我终于理解了。 = After hearing the explanation, I finally understood.
- 互相理解很重要。 = Understanding each other is important.

mnemonic: It is composed of 口 (mouth) and 曷. The 口 radical hints at an action of the mouth. Be careful! Unlike Japanese 薬を飲む, in Chinese you 'eat' medicine: 吃药 (chīyào).
examples: - 请多喝水。 = Please drink more water.
- 我和朋友喝了茶。 = I drank tea with my friend.
- 晚上我不喝酒。 = I don't drink alcohol at night.
- 我不喝咖啡，喝茶。 = I don't drink coffee, I drink tea.

mnemonic: It is composed of 喜 (joy) and 欢 (happy). Think of it as 'finding joy in something'. Unlike Japanese 好き, 喜欢 is a real verb and takes the object directly: 我喜欢猫. It can also take a verb: 我喜欢喝茶. For 'love', use 爱 (ài).
examples: - 我喜欢猫。 = I like cats.
- 我朋友喜欢音乐。 = My friend likes music.
- 我非常喜欢日本料理。 = I really like Japanese food.
- 我开始喜欢他了。 = I have started to like him.

tr: （duō）- To be many, to be much
mnemonic: It is composed of two 夕 (evening) stacked up. Think of it as 'many evenings piled up'. Be careful! 多 can't directly modify a noun: say 很多人 (many people), not 多人. Its opposite is 少 (shǎo), 'few'.
examples: - 日本有很多山。 = There are many mountains in Japan.
- 今天作业很多。 = There is a lot of homework today.
- 车站里人很多。 = The station has a lot of people.
- 今年的雨比去年多。 = There was more rain this year than last year.

mnemonic: Think of 去 as someone leaving the spot where they stand. 去 means 'to go (away from here)', and its opposite is 来 (lái), 'to come'. Use 过 for experience: 去过韩国, 'have been to Korea'.
examples: - 我去学校。 = I go to school.
- 明天我和朋友去海边。 = Tomorrow I'm going to the beach with friends.
- 我去过韩国。 = I have been to Korea.
- 我们一起去吧。 = Let's go together.

mnemonic: It is composed of 直 (straight) and 接 (connect). Think of it as 'connecting in a straight line'. Where Korean says 직접적, Chinese just uses 直接 (no 的 needed). Its opposite is 间接 (jiànjiē), 'indirect'.
examples: - 太直接的说法有时不礼貌。 = Overly direct phrasing is sometimes impolite.
- 他直接问了我。 = He asked me directly.
- 直接原因是下雨。 = The direct cause is the rain.
- 中文常常使用间接的表达。 = Chinese often uses indirect expressions.

mnemonic: It is composed of 特 (special) and 定 (fix). Think of it as 'fixed on something special'. For the verb 'to determine', use 确定 (quèdìng), and 'to pinpoint' is 锁定 (suǒdìng). Same characters as the Japanese 特定.
examples: - 只有特定的人可以进入。 = Only specific people can enter.
- 我们需要在特定的时间见面。 = We need to meet at a specific time.
- 警方锁定了嫌疑人。 = The police have pinpointed the suspect.
- 很难确定地点。 = It is hard to determine the location.

mnemonic: It is composed of 不 (not) and 吉利 (lucky). Think of it as 'not lucky'. For 'ominous', 不祥 (bùxiáng) is also used. Remember: 4 (sì) sounds like 死 (sǐ, die) and is unlucky, while 8 (bā) sounds like 发 (fā, prosper) and is lucky.
examples: - 据说黑猫不吉利。 = It is said that black cats are unlucky.
- 四是不吉利的数字。 = Four is an unlucky number.
- 我做了一个不吉利的梦。 = I had an ominous dream.
- 我有一种不祥的预感。 = I have an ominous feeling.

mnemonic: It is composed of 不 (not) and 同 (same). Think of it as 'not the same'. The everyday version is 不一样 (bù yíyàng). Be careful! 不同 only means 'different'. For 'wrong', say 不对 (búduì), and 不 changes to bú before a 4th tone.
examples: - 我的意见和他不同。 = My opinion is different from his.
- 不同的国家有不同的文化。 = Different countries have different cultures.
- 汉语和韩语有一点不一样。 = Chinese and Korean are a little different.
- 那样不对。 = That's wrong.

mnemonic: It is composed of 不 (not) and 方便 (convenient). 方 is 'way' and 便 is 'easy', so think of it as 'not an easy way'. 方便 is also used politely to ask about someone's availability: 你什么时候方便？ 'When are you free?'
examples: - 这个镇火车很少，很不方便。 = This town has few trains, so it's very inconvenient.
- 我家附近没有商店，很不方便。 = There are no shops near my home, so it's inconvenient.
- 旧手机不方便用。 = The old phone is inconvenient to use.
- 我习惯了不方便的生活。 = I got used to an inconvenient life.

mnemonic: It is composed of 这 (this) and 样 (way/manner). It belongs to a family: 这样 (like this), 那样 (like that), 怎样 (how). In speech it is often said as 这么样, and 这么 (zhème) is used before adjectives: 这么大, 'this big'.
examples: - 结果是这样的。 = The result is like this.
- 这样做就很简单。 = It's easy if you do it this way.
- 问题是这样的。 = The problem is like this.
- 我不能这样下去。 = I can't go on like this.

mnemonic: It is composed of 语言 (language) and 的 (the particle that turns a word into a modifier). Think of it as 'language-related'. 的 is the Chinese source of the suffix seen in Japanese 〜的 and Korean 〜적. For 'non-verbal', say 非语言 (fēi yǔyán).
examples: - 语言上的差异很大。 = The linguistic differences are large.
- 这个孩子的语言能力很强。 = This child has strong language ability.
- 非语言交流也很重要。 = Non-verbal communication is also important.
- 这不是语言问题。 = This is not a language problem.

mnemonic: It is composed of 有 (have) and 趣 (interest). Think of it as 'having interest'. The more colloquial version is 有意思 (yǒu yìsi). To say 'to be interested in', use 感兴趣 (gǎn xìngqù).
examples: - 这个故事很有趣。 = This story is very interesting.
- 我读了一本有趣的书。 = I read an interesting book.
- 他的研究很有意思。 = His research is interesting.
- 我觉得日本历史很有意思。 = I think Japanese history is fascinating.
